clue.text: What open doors and often don't close, shock horror!

definitions.text: What open doors and often don't close, shock horror!

parts.words: What open doors and often don't close, shock horror!
parts.note: the clue reads like a list of things that open but will not shut; read again, a shock is a head of hair and the horror is hairs whose tips have frayed open and stay that way

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that opens doors and then won't shut, ending in mock alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a mass of hair, and the 'horror' is the hairdresser's complaint: tips that have opened up and stay apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair damage where the tips fray apart is the classic grooming horror, and those frayed tips have opened and never close again.

clue.text: Home supporter catches cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the last letter of the word round to the front

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A sports fan from the home side makes catches while out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final S of NAILS to the front. 'Home supporter' looks like a football fan, but it is a creature that carries its house on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: this garden mollusc holds up its shell, its home, wherever it goes.

clue.text: Dip in road brings up food

indicators.note: in places the dip within the road

parts.note: a lane is a minor road
a sag is a dip or droop

explanation.surface: A dip in the road throws up something to eat, perhaps from a jolted lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: This layered Italian pasta bake is a common dish, so food is its broad category.

clue.text: Test clothes, chance to go over line

definitions.meaning: to see whether garments fit before buying them
an attempt to get away with something, pushing past what is acceptable, as in 'it was a cheeky attempt'

explanation.surface: A rugby image: testing a chance to cross the line and score.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture of a try over the line is a distraction; the second sense is the informal noun for an attempt to see what one can get away with.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both fitting garments on and, as a noun, a bold attempt to overstep the mark.

clue.text: They don't make theatre bookings — and their excuse?

definitions.text: They don't make theatre bookings — and their excuse?

parts.words: They don't make theatre bookings — and their excuse?
parts.note: people who book seats and never turn up; their excuse could be that there were no performances on

explanation.surface: A grumble about people who skip theatre bookings and the excuses they give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' means turn up for, not create; the excuse is the second reading of the phrase: there were no performances.
explanation.definitionFit: People who book and then fail to turn up are absentees, and the phrase also reads as 'there were no performances'.

clue.text: Split up and get grease monkeys around

indicators.note: to monkey around is to fool about, so the letters are messed about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to divide up and fetch the oil for the mechanics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grease monkeys' looks like a phrase for mechanics, but 'monkeys around' is the signal to rearrange GET GREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate people into groups kept apart from each other is to divide them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Loud weapon that's more than stable!

parts.note: f is the musical marking forte, loud
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A noisy gun that seems steadier than steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' reads as an adjective, but it is the horse building; a whole agricultural holding is more than a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: an agricultural holding includes stables and much more besides.

clue.text: Sympathise with price that's hilarious in retrospect

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

indicators.note: looking back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: ROFL is the internet shorthand 'rolling on the floor laughing', for something hilarious

explanation.surface: Looking back, a charge seems laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel compassion toward someone's troubles is to share their pain, the phrasal verb's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Correct parasol's opening with drunk reclined outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the single letter
drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy lying back under a parasol, putting it up correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges RECLINED into REDENCIL, and 'outside' puts that around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors mark errors with this tool, so as a verb it means to amend or censor text.

clue.text: Help on the way (cases yet to be resolved)

indicators.note: resolved here means broken up and reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Help is coming, though the outstanding legal cases are still to be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help on the way' sounds like rescue coming; the way is the road itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective road studs guide drivers at night, literally an aid set into the road surface.

clue.text: Grabbing cloudy drinks each day for starters

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a cloudy sky is grey

indicators.note: the starters are the opening letters of the words

explanation.surface: Someone downing cloudy drinks every day, starting early.
explanation.definitionFit: Grabbing behaviour is acquisitive and wanting more than one's share, a close synonym.

clue.text: Slump forward into bottle

parts.note: to flag is to tire or droop
on means forward, as in 'move on'

explanation.surface: Someone slumping forward onto a bottle, perhaps after too much drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vessel for wine or ale with a handle and spout, a kind of bottle or jug.

clue.text: Relentless nympho?

definitions.meaning: happening in succession without a pause
someone who takes lovers in an endless succession, man upon man

explanation.walkthrough: The query flags the second reading as playful: a person with an insatiable appetite takes partners in unbroken sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in continuous succession, which describes both an unremitting series and a string of lovers.

clue.text: When bongs were used by day nurse

parts.note: the Big Ben bongs opened ITV's evening bulletin 'News at Ten', so the bongs sounded at that hour

explanation.surface: A nurse who works days in a hospital where bongs are used.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a British evening TV news programme that opens with the chimes of Big Ben.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to care for them, to look after them, which is one sense of the verb.

clue.text: Unfortunately, these euro coins build up

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly, these coins in the European currency are piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build up' looks like money accumulating, but it means a structure built high up, in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a children's den constructed among branches is a building up off the ground.

clue.text: Checking out will hide what's wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal will that conceals wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking out' is slang for dying and 'will' is desire, not the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire to die, to check out of life, is a self-destructive urge; 'will' here means a wish.

clue.text: Green leaves, having pretended Brighton's good

parts.note: sham means feigned or pretended
Brighton rock is a hard stick candy sold at the English seaside resort; a 'good' is a piece of merchandise

explanation.surface: Someone faking that Brighton's green leaves are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside town famous for its sticks of rock, a hard candy.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-lobed clover, Ireland's emblem, is a plant with green leaves.

clue.text: Craft enabled landfall short of France, the ultimate target

indicators.note: to craft is to shape, so the letters are fashioned into a new arrangement
short of means lacking, so the letter goes from the fodder

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A boat is able to land, falling short of France, its intended destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat but is the anagram signal; 'short of France' removes F from ENABLED LANDFALL before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the supreme or most important thing, the final goal everything is aimed at.

clue.text: Ladies, perhaps, kind to kick off date's brief search

parts.note: the Ladies is a women's toilet, one kind of loo

indicators.note: kick off means start, so the first letter is taken
brief cuts the word short by its final letter

parts.note: dates means sees, as in going out with someone

explanation.surface: A woman nipping to the toilet before a date for a quick check.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British for toilet. 'brief' drops the last S of SEES.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase means a quick look around, a cursory inspection or survey.

clue.text: Had mate coming up with ideas regularly for Spurs v Arsenal etc

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: bred means mated and had offspring

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A breeder's ideas about a football rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur (Spurs) and Arsenal are north London football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A match between local rival teams from the same area is a local derby, of which this fixture is one.

clue.text: See 16
In Berlin, the wet parts becoming drier

indicators.note: parts means splits, so the word opens to take another inside

parts.note: der is German for the
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: In Berlin, the rainy districts are drying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun but is a verb: the German article splits to take RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack where washed dishes drip dry, so one that makes them drier.

clue.text: See 11
Trouble surrendering is a slight difference

indicators.note: surrendering means giving up, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: a nuisance is trouble or bother

explanation.surface: Giving in causes trouble that makes only a little difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle shade of meaning or tone is a small distinction, the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Explosive start (I must be delayed)

indicators.note: delayed means it comes later, so the letter is moved further along

parts.note: an intro is the start of something

explanation.surface: An explosive kick-off, with the speaker insisting on a postponement.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for nitroglycerine, a powerful liquid explosive used in dynamite.

clue.text: Best sheets about to be put on

indicators.note: in a down entry, put on means placed on top of the other piece

parts.note: c is circa, about
a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: The finest bed linen is about to be put on.
explanation.definitionFit: The top part of milk, figuratively the elite: the best of a group.

clue.text: With empty menu, enjoys linguini for breakfast

indicators.note: an empty word loses its insides, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A diner faced with a bare menu is happy to have pasta for breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit, typically eaten as the morning meal.

clue.text: With 11 21, it'd mean new wheels

indicators.note: wheels means turns about, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Riding one behind the other would mean buying a new bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the definition. 'new wheels' looks like a bicycle, and a two-seater bicycle does put riders one behind the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders on a two-seater bicycle sit in line, so the phrase means in succession, one behind the next.

clue.text: Abandon future plant, possibly in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a seed may grow into a plant

explanation.surface: A gardener talking about giving up on a would-be plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a right is to surrender it, a synonym of abandon.

clue.text: Bloke's weight is entertaining to chart

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the outer piece holds the other

parts.note: his means belonging to a bloke
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A man's weight is amusing to plot on a graph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like 'amusing' but means 'holding': HIS and GRAM take in TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar diagram of frequency distributions is a type of statistical graph.
